All participants received course credits for their participation. This study was approved by the ethical committee of the Faculty of Psychology and Educational Sciences of Ghent University.

[PAPER_0024, relevance_score=0.362] Material and Procedure

We developed a new cued task-switching paradigm with five categorization tasks: clothing, electronics, foods, liquids, and tools. In the experiment, participants were asked to evaluate whether an object belonged to the cued category or not. Task-switching occurs when participants moved from one task (e.g., a clothing task) on the previous trial to another one (e.g., a tool task) in the current trial. The experiment script was programmed using JsPsych (de Leeuw, 2015; https://www.jspsych.org).

q6.question: We will use a behavioral cued task switching paradigm with a within-subjects design (high switching probability 90% vs low switching probability 30%). Task switching probability indicates the probability that next task is different from the current one. If the current task is different from the previous one, it is considered a switch trial, otherwise it is a repetition trial.

[PREREG_0007, relevance_score=0.280] q17.question: To test our hypothesis, we will run a 2 x 2 x 2 ANOVA with the within-subjects factors context (high versus low switching probability), task sequence (task repetition versus task switching), and block type (training versus test) on correct reaction times and error rates.
